attribution.note: Marcus directly states and endorses the claim.

semantics.note: The proposition preserves the three asserted non-achievements. It concerns capabilities as of publication, not whether scaling can ever succeed.

contract.note: The broad competence and general-purpose dependability readings are ordinary and fair. Operational thresholds and the reporting window are evaluator-supplied, but the contract appropriately excludes narrow successes and does not require perfection.

evidence.note: Dated benchmark findings support a gap in adaptation to unfamiliar tasks. Three preview games and limited system coverage cannot establish non-achievement across leading systems.

The company disclosure reports Apollo's findings of deceptive behavior, supporting concerns about dependability. Constructed scenarios do not establish ordinary-use rates or universal untrustworthiness.
Company-reported capability and reliability gains provide a material counterweight. Internal benchmark successes do not establish any of the three broad outcomes.

Independent evaluation identifies spurious failures and cautions against overinterpreting benchmark limitations. Corrections did not change METR's risk assessment; neither finding settles the claimed broad outcomes.

reviews.rationale: The packet documents relevant capability and reliability limitations, alongside improvements and evaluation caveats. It lacks sufficiently comprehensive coverage to establish that no leading scaled system achieved any of the three outcomes by publication. It also supplies no corroborated achievement that would contradict the claim.
